ConvoyTileCalculator.kt:75:     * ZOOMSLOT-2026-08-10D: THE DOWNLOAD ZOOM RULE. Satellite to z18, rendered maps to z16.
ConvoyTileCalculator.kt:77:     * Economics, not capability: each level quadruples the tile count. Above z18
ConvoyTileCalculator.kt:78:     * satellite imagery in open country is upscaled rather than sharper, and
ConvoyTileCalculator.kt:79:     * above z16 a topo map has said everything it has to say - contours do not

ConvoyTileCalculator.kt:88:     * An empty slot means NO CAP - see the note on corridorTiles.

ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:376:private fun fmtTiles(n: Int): String = "%,d".format(n)
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:379: * PHASE0-QUEUE-PANEL-2026-07-24 - ETA PLACEHOLDER. Returns null today (line 3 hidden).
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:381: * PHASE 1 implements this from THE LAST 2 COMPLETED DOWNLOADS (Fred's spec):
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:382: * once QueueEntry carries `completedAt` alongside its existing `createdAt`,
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:383: * each completed entry yields a real observed rate of
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:384: * downloadedTiles / (completedAt - createdAt). Averaging the last 2 smooths
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:385: * the estimate, survives app restarts (persisted in the entry, not held in
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:386: * memory), and does NOT jitter with connectivity the way instantaneous
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:387: * throughput sampling does - which matters on trails where the link drops.
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:389: * Until then this returns null so line 3 does not render. Do NOT substitute a
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:390: * live-rate estimate here: an unstable number is worse than none.
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:392: * RETURNS Pair(duration, completionStamp) - BOTH go on line 3, because they
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:393: * answer different questions. Duration ("how long do I wait?") is what you
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:394: * want for a short job; a completion stamp ("when will it be done?") is what
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:395: * you want for a long one, because "31h 15m" forces arithmetic while you are
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:396: * standing in a parking lot. A corridor job at ~894,507 tiles can genuinely
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:397: * run into DAYS, so bare minutes are useless.
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:399: * DURATION - resolve to days/hours/minutes, NEVER bare minutes:
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:401: * COMPLETION STAMP - reuse the existing `dateFmt` ("MMM d h:mm a"):
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:404: * ROUND LONG ESTIMATES. A two-sample rate cannot justify minute precision: if
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:405: * it is off by 30%, a 30-hour job's stated finish is wrong by NINE HOURS. Keep
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:406: * the "~" prefix and round anything over ~8 hours to the nearest hour so it
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:407: * does not read as a promise.
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:409: * @param tilesRemaining active-remaining + queued total
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:410: * @return Pair("3h 20m", "Jul 26 6:40 PM"), or null when no rate is known yet
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:412:private fun fmtDuration(totalSec: Long): String {
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:422: * ETA-ONERATE-2026-08-09H: THE rate. One definition, used for the number on screen and
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:423: * for the completion estimate, so the two cannot disagree.
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:425: * Sums the running jobs rather than reading one of them: per-job tiles/sec
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:426: * FALLS as slots are added, because each job takes a smaller share of the same
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:427: * pipe, so a single row reads like a regression when throughput is actually up.
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:430:private fun liveRate(entries: List<QueueEntry>): Double =
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:431:    entries.filter { it.status == QueueStatus.DOWNLOADING }.sumOf { e ->
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:432:        val began = if (e.startedAt > 0L) e.startedAt else e.createdAt
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:433:        val secs = if (began > 0L)
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:434:            (System.currentTimeMillis() - began) / 1000.0 else 0.0
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:435:        if (secs > 0.0) e.downloadedTiles / secs else 0.0
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:439: * ETA-ONERATE-2026-08-09H: tiles remaining divided by the rate ALREADY ON SCREEN.
ConvoyDownloadQueuePanel.kt:441: * This function used to compute its own rate from every completed entry over

ArtifactSearch.kt:1:package com.geeksville.mesh.convoy
ArtifactSearch.kt:4: * Reusable, DB-free helpers for artifact name-search results.
ArtifactSearch.kt:8: * Artifact names are NOT unique: the same name can occur on many artifacts with
ArtifactSearch.kt:9: * different geometry (e.g. on device, "Bluff Trail" x5, "9 Line Trail" x11, each
ArtifactSearch.kt:10: * a distinct geom_hash). A search result is therefore a *name-occurrence keyed by
ArtifactSearch.kt:11: * geom_hash*, not just a name. Rather than show the raw 64-char SHA-256 hash in a
ArtifactSearch.kt:12: * cramped list, we show a small per-name SEQUENCE NUMBER. The full geom_hash and
ArtifactSearch.kt:13: * id still travel on every row for the detail card / FIT.
ArtifactSearch.kt:15: * This file is pure -- no DB handle, no Compose -- so the numbering transform can
ArtifactSearch.kt:16: * be reused anywhere name+geom_hash rows need stable display numbering: search
ArtifactSearch.kt:17: * results, a maintenance/list screen, the alias accordion, etc.
ArtifactSearch.kt:20: * RULES BAKED INTO assignNameSequence() -- read before reusing or changing:
ArtifactSearch.kt:22: *  R1. SEQUENCE IS PER-NAME, NOT GLOBAL. Numbering restarts at 1 for each
ArtifactSearch.kt:23: *      distinct name. So two "Bluff Trail" rows are #1 and #2; an unrelated
ArtifactSearch.kt:24: *      "Aspen Trail" right after is #1 again -- not a continuation of the list.
ArtifactSearch.kt:26: *  R2. ORDER WITHIN A NAME IS BY geom_hash (ascending, lexicographic). This is
ArtifactSearch.kt:27: *      what makes the number STABLE: a given geometry always sorts to the same
ArtifactSearch.kt:28: *      relative position among its same-name siblings, so its number does not
ArtifactSearch.kt:29: *      change between searches, app launches, or devices (the hash is content-
ArtifactSearch.kt:30: *      derived). The number is a stable proxy for the hash.
ArtifactSearch.kt:32: *  R3. SELF-SORTING. The function sorts internally; callers may pass rows in any
ArtifactSearch.kt:33: *      order and still get correct, deterministic numbers. Sort key =
ArtifactSearch.kt:34: *      (name lower-cased, geom_hash). The lower-casing MUST match searchByName's
ArtifactSearch.kt:35: *      SQL `ORDER BY name COLLATE NOCASE, geom_hash` so on-device display order
ArtifactSearch.kt:36: *      and the numbering always agree. If you change one, change the other.
ArtifactSearch.kt:38: *  R4. NAME-GROUP IDENTITY IS EXACT (case-sensitive) STRING EQUALITY. The sort
ArtifactSearch.kt:39: *      is case-insensitive (R3) but a *group boundary* is an exact-string change.
ArtifactSearch.kt:40: *      So "Foo" and "foo" -- if both existed -- sort adjacent yet number as two
ArtifactSearch.kt:41: *      separate groups (each starting at 1), which is correct: they are
ArtifactSearch.kt:42: *      genuinely different names.
ArtifactSearch.kt:44: *  R5. NULL HANDLING. Null name -> "Not Named"; null geom_hash -> "" (an empty
ArtifactSearch.kt:45: *      hash sorts first within its name group); null type -> "". NOTE: the
ArtifactSearch.kt:46: *      search QUERY already excludes "Not Named"/blank names, so in the search
ArtifactSearch.kt:47: *      path these defaults rarely fire -- they exist so the util is safe for
ArtifactSearch.kt:48: *      OTHER callers that may pass unfiltered rows.
ArtifactSearch.kt:50: *  R6. ROWS WITHOUT AN id ARE DROPPED. A result must be openable in the detail
ArtifactSearch.kt:51: *      card, which needs the id; an id-less row is unusable, so it is filtered
ArtifactSearch.kt:52: *      out rather than shown.
ArtifactSearch.kt:54: *  R7. INPUT CONTRACT. Each input row is a Map<String,String?> carrying at least
ArtifactSearch.kt:55: *      the keys "id", "name", "geom_hash", "type" (exactly the keys produced by
ArtifactSearch.kt:56: *      SpatialDbManager.searchByName). Extra keys are ignored.
ArtifactSearch.kt:59: * Rules baked into the QUERY (SpatialDbManager.searchByName) -- documented here
ArtifactSearch.kt:60: * for the full picture, but enforced there, not in this file:
ArtifactSearch.kt:61: *  Q1. NON-SPATIAL: searches the whole table, NOT the map viewport (unlike the
ArtifactSearch.kt:62: *      queryXByViewport family). A match can be far off-screen. FIT (later) is
ArtifactSearch.kt:63: *      the only bridge back to the bbox-scoped display.
ArtifactSearch.kt:64: *  Q2. SUBSTRING match: `name LIKE '%term%'` (finds the term anywhere in a name).
ArtifactSearch.kt:65: *  Q3. EXCLUDES unnamed rows: name not null, not blank, and <> 'Not Named'.
ArtifactSearch.kt:66: *  Q4. CAPPED at `limit` (default 200). A caller can detect truncation by
ArtifactSearch.kt:67: *      comparing result size to the limit and prompt the user to refine.
ArtifactSearch.kt:70:/** One numbered search/list result. seq = stable per-name sequence (1-based). */

ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:854:     * WHY THIS EXISTS. enqueueRefresh above derives a bbox from the store's
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:855:     * EXTENT and chops that rectangle into grid cells. Coverage in two distant
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:856:     * places makes a rectangle spanning both, and every empty cell in between
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:857:     * still becomes a job: 3,287 of them on 08-11, with an ETA of 194 days.
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:859:     * Here a quadrant is COUNTED before it is queued, and dropped when it holds
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:860:     * nothing. Disjoint coverage therefore stays disjoint by construction rather
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:861:     * than by inference, and totalTiles is the STORED count so the estimate is

ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:864:     * The worker needs no change: it already filters refresh jobs to hasTile, so
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:865:     * a tile you do not hold is never fetched. What was wrong was queueing the
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:866:     * ground at all.
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:868:     * Submitted as MAP_SOURCE_REFRESH -- the existing type. No enum change, so
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:869:     * nothing can break a queue file already persisted on a device.
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:871:     * Corridor shape survives because nothing here infers shape: the tiles being
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:872:     * refreshed ARE the corridor. And with replace-in-place the old tile stays
ConvoyDownloadQueue.kt:873:     * until the new one lands, so coverage never drops while it runs.

ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:242:     * SEGMENTATION SPLITTER  (replaces fixed-12-mile gridCells)
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:244:     * Splits one drawn bbox into ceil(realTotal / 50_000) roughly-equal cells so
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:245:     * no single download job strands a queue slot. Each cell is a FULL z-stack
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:246:     * slice (z10..z18) of its geography -> every cell same shape of work ->
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:247:     * comparable -> they finish together in parallel slots = load balancing.
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:250:     * WHY sizeTiles is passed IN (not just quickEstimate here):
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:251:     *   quickEstimate(bbox).tileCount = ONE LAYER's geographic tiles.
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:252:     *   SAT actually pulls THREE layers (base + 2 overlays) over the SAME
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:253:     *   geography, each a separate download. So the REAL job volume for SAT is
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:254:     *   quickEstimate * 3 (~24,716 * 3 = ~74,148). enqueueArea already knows the
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:255:     *   per-slot layer count (slotLayers), so it passes the REAL total in as
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:256:     *   sizeTiles. Sizing off the bare 1-layer number under-segments (this was
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:257:     *   caught by the dry-run JSON on 2026-07-11: a 74K SAT area reported 24,716
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:258:     *   and split into 1 segment when it needed 2).
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:260:     * WHY overlap is TILE-WIDTHS and SEAM-ONLY (not a fixed degree amount):
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:261:     *   Overlap only exists to stop a boundary-straddling tile from falling into
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:263:     *   1 tile at z18 = 360 / 2^18 = 0.00137 deg. The original spec used 1/8 deg
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:264:     *   (0.125) = ~91 tiles/edge, which BALLOONED a 24K area to 155K (6x) in the
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:266:     *   applied ONLY when numSegments>1 (a single segment has no internal seam,
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:267:     *   so it gets ZERO pad and reports its true tile count).
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:269:     * Returns the SAME [north,south,east,west] DoubleArray shape gridCells
ConvoyTileDownloader.kt:270:     * returned, so the enqueue loop in enqueueArea is UNCHANGED.

RiderTrailScanner.kt:8: * was 2 pieces of new ground; this version gives 2 pieces, 32.6 mi, all joined. Four changes, all here:
RiderTrailScanner.kt:9: *   1. the track is filled in to [DENSE_M] before matching (onX records 30-700 m apart -- jumps skipped junctions);
RiderTrailScanner.kt:10: *   2. "on a trail" = within [NEAR_M] of the trail's LINE (was: of a node), and the join snaps onto that line;
RiderTrailScanner.kt:11: *   3. direction = over [BEAR_WIN_M] of track either side (was [SMOOTH] points -- 200 m to over 1 km on onX);
RiderTrailScanner.kt:12: *   4. a trail segment is indexed in EVERY grid cell its box touches (was: its midpoint's cell only).

RiderTrailScanner.kt:14: * ⚠ CORRECTION 10-09 (afternoon): the "proven" figures above were TRACK AGAINST TRACK -- the harness used a second
RiderTrailScanner.kt:15: *   recording of Broken Ridge as the network, never the real trails. Against the real trails release g still left
RiderTrailScanner.kt:16: *   16 gaps (up to 135 m) -- see RIDERRULES below.
RiderTrailScanner.kt:18: * RIDERRULES-2026-10-09 (Fred): THE AGREED PROCESS, NOTHING ELSE. Overlay the track's polyline on the trails; every
RiderTrailScanner.kt:19: * stretch where it leaves the trails and comes back to a trail is ONE piece, joined at both ends. The old process's
RiderTrailScanner.kt:21: * no minimum length for a connector (MIN_RUN_M 150 m threw away exactly the short connectors riders were missing).
RiderTrailScanner.kt:22: *   - ONE tolerance: [NEAR_M] -- the polyline within 20 m of a trail's line is ON that trail (GPS error).
RiderTrailScanner.kt:23: *   - Fred's rule for the tiny ones: a piece joined at both ends and shorter than [TINY_M] (10 m) is written ONLY if
RiderTrailScanner.kt:24: *     it is the only connection -- different trails at its two ends that do not already meet there. Same trail at
RiderTrailScanner.kt:25: *     both ends (the GPS wandered off and back) or two trails that already meet -> skipped.
RiderTrailScanner.kt:26: *   - [MIN_RUN_M] stays ONLY for a piece NOT joined at both ends (a dead end or open ground), so GPS wander out in
RiderTrailScanner.kt:27: *     the open is not laid down as trail.
RiderTrailScanner.kt:28: * MEASURED off-device, 10-09, against the REAL trails around Broken Ridge (Fred's PC copy spatial_0909.db: 251
RiderTrailScanner.kt:29: * trails; the 105 old rider stubs left out as the clear leaves them; written pieces fed back as network, as scanAll

ConvoySourceMigration.kt:14: * The durable record of a map-source change.
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:16: * A source change on a column is destructive in two ways at once: it deletes
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:17: * the column's .mbtiles stores (GB scale, no backup) and it clears the
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:18: * download queue history that would otherwise say what had been downloaded.
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:19: * Afterwards nothing in the app can answer "what did I have, and where did it
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:20: * go?" - so this object writes that answer down BEFORE the deletion starts.
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:22: * It doubles as the in-progress sentinel. The outgoing source's cache dirs are
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:23: * only knowable while that source is still assigned to the slot; once
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:24: * MapSourceManager.updateSlotSource has run they are gone from every live
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:25: * structure. begin() must therefore be called BEFORE updateSlotSource, or the
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:26: * label stores (SAT_LABELS_PLACES, SAT_LABELS_TRANSPORT - 461 MB on a measured
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:27: * device) become orphans that nothing knows to remove.
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:29: * A file with no completed_at is an interrupted migration. Resume is a
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:30: * deliberate prompt, never automatic: finishing means deleting GB of tiles,
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:31: * and the launch that discovers it may be at a trailhead.
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:33: * Location is maps/source_changes/ - a SIBLING of maps/tiles/, chosen so that
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:34: * clearing a column can never destroy the record of that clear. Nothing that
ConvoySourceMigration.kt:35: * deletes tiles should ever walk this directory.

SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:58: * ═══ THE FOUR WRONG TURNS, and why the code looks like this ═══
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:60: * ⛔ 1. DISTANCE MUST NOT BE IN THE SCORE. The first search scored
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:61: *    `poiValue - miles * 0.06`, which is a CHEAPEST-PATH search wearing a POI
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:62: *    bonus. It returned 5 features on 69 miles and NO SPRINGS AT ALL though
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:63: *    springs were 22 of the 39 available. Fred: "point value should be the
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:64: *    winner." ⭐ MILES ARE A BUDGET, NEVER A COST. Score the features; spend
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:65: *    miles until the budget runs out. `scoreSet()` takes no distance argument
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:68: * ⛔ 2. PENALISE, DO NOT FILTER. Generating thousands of candidates, ranking
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:69: *    them, then filtering for distinctness returns ONE route — on a corridor
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:70: *    with a shared spine every candidate shares it. Navigation apps do the
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:71: *    opposite: find the best, PENALISE its edges, re-solve. The second route is
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:72: *    then the best route that AVOIDS the first. See `penalty` below.
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:74: * ⛔ 3. RANK, DO NOT PRE-CONSTRAIN. Searching inside a narrow band strangled it
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:75: *    before it found anything. Explore to the ceiling, score, then apply the
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:76: *    rider's band as a CUTOFF on the results.
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:78: * ⛔ 4. THE GREEDY RUNS TO THE CEILING. With one target distance every restart
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:79: *    produced the same length. ⭐ Each restart draws its OWN target from the
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:80: *    range, so the pool spans it.
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:83: * makes every scoring corridor too expensive and the search returns the best
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:84: * REMAINING route, which visits nothing — two routes came back score 0.0 on
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:85: * 08-22. TWO GOOD ROUTES BEAT FOUR PADDED ONES.
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:89: * COVERAGE IS ~12 MILES PER FEATURE, NEAR-LINEAR, NO KNEE. All 39 features in
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:90: * the Arizona Strip were reachable — at 448.7 miles. So a 60-mile ride reaching
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:91: * 4 features is what the corridor COSTS, not a bug. The panel says so.
SHARED:route/GtRoute.kt:94: * degree-4 nodes climb to 85% by 50 ft, which is parallel tracks being WELDED
